stories.orgs: Tennessee Aquarium Conservation Institute; Conservation Fisheries Inc.; U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service (Dale Hollow and Wolf Creek National Fish Hatcheries); Tennessee Wildlife Resources Agency
stories.desc: The Tennessee Aquarium Conservation Institute has worked on the endangered Barrens topminnow since 2001 with Knoxville-based Conservation Fisheries, monitoring the few remaining wild spring-fed populations on the Barrens Plateau. Partners have propagated and released more than 44,000 topminnows and have rescued fish from springs threatened by prolonged drought. Assurance colonies are also held at Dale Hollow and Wolf Creek National Fish Hatcheries; expanding wild reintroduction depends on securing more publicly owned spring sites.
stories.water: Spring-fed headwaters of the Barrens Plateau (Duck and Collins river headwaters)
stories.notes: Middle Tennessee (Barrens Plateau), not East Tennessee; included because the slice covers Tennessee fish reintroduction statewide. Coordinates approximate and represent the species' range centroid.

stories.title: Blue Spring Creek Livestock Exclusion and Riparian BMPs
stories.orgs: USDA Natural Resources Conservation Service; Coffee County Soil Conservation District; Tennessee Department of Agriculture; USEPA Section 319 program; participating farmers
stories.desc: Farmers installed exclusion fencing to keep livestock off streambanks, frost-free alternative watering tanks, geotextile stabilization of heavy-use soil around ponds, animal waste holding ponds, and pasture seeding under a nutrient management plan. Between 1999 and 2003 EPT families rose from 6 to 11, total taxa from 15 to 25, and the habitat score climbed from 114 to 136 against a target of 123. Blue Spring Creek was removed from Tennessee's 303(d) list in 2004.
stories.sector: Partnership (federal, state, local district, private landowners)
stories.notes: Middle Tennessee. Total project cost $110,219. Lat/lon approximate; nearest town not named in the source.

stories.title: East Rock Creek Watershed Restoration, Rock Creek (Duck River basin)
stories.orgs: The Nature Conservancy; Tennessee Department of Agriculture; Tennessee Department of Environment and Conservation; Center for Watershed Protection; USDA Natural Resources Conservation Service; Austin Peay State University; Marshall County School District; City of Lewisburg; Marshall and Bedford county soil conservation districts
lpOrgs: Tennessee Department of Environment and Conservation
stories.desc: The Nature Conservancy led Section 319 grants that put agricultural BMPs across the Rock Creek watershed — 66 cover-crop practices on 2,547 acres, 16,002 feet of fencing, 600 feet of riparian forest buffer, 252 acres of forage planting, 452 acres of cropland conversion, 10,515 feet of livestock pipeline, 15 heavy-use areas and 19 watering facilities — plus 101 state-funded BMPs along East Rock Creek and its tributaries. The macroinvertebrate index rose from 24 in 2011 to 34 in 2015, above the passing score of 32, and about 14.17 miles of East Rock Creek were significantly improved by 2018. The creek was removed from Tennessee's 2018 impaired waters list for nitrate, siltation and habitat alterations.
stories.water: East Rock Creek (Big Rock Creek, Duck River basin)
stories.notes: Middle Tennessee. Remains impaired for E. coli from pasture grazing as of 2018. Lat/lon approximate.

stories.title: Sequatchie River Livestock Management and Septic Repairs
stories.orgs: Southeast Tennessee Resource Conservation and Development Council; Bledsoe, Grundy, Marion and Sequatchie County Soil Conservation Districts; Tennessee Department of Agriculture; Tennessee Department of Environment and Conservation; University of the South; USDA Natural Resources Conservation Service; Tennessee Wildlife Resources Agency; Tennessee Valley Authority; City of Dunlap
lpOrgs: Tennessee Department of Environment and Conservation
stories.desc: On the main stem Sequatchie River, partners installed cross-fencing for rotational grazing and riparian fencing to keep livestock out of the stream and repaired two failing septic systems under a 2013-2015 Section 319 grant, while the state cost-share program funded 33 further agricultural practices including exclusion fencing, alternative watering facilities and heavy-use areas from 2004 onward. The E. coli geometric mean at river mile 41.5 fell from 424.6 CFU/100 mL in 2006 to 121.1 CFU/100 mL in 2010-2011, below the 126 CFU/100 mL standard. TDEC removed a 23.1-mile segment from the impaired waters list in 2014 as fully supporting all designated uses.
stories.notes: Sequatchie Valley is in the East Tennessee grand division but west of the Knoxville-eastward river list in the slice definition. Coordinates approximate (river mile 41.5 near Dunlap).

stories.title: Upper Citico Creek Dam Removal
stories.orgs: American Rivers; U.S. Forest Service (Cherokee National Forest); U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service
stories.desc: A 7-foot-tall, 35-foot-long concrete barrier built in 1966 was removed from Citico Creek in the Cherokee National Forest in October 2015. The dam had been built to keep stocked non-native fish out of the creek but blocked 52 native fish species from upstream spawning habitat. Removal reconnected historic trout habitat, restored natural sediment and gravel transport, and eliminated a passage barrier for three federally endangered species - the Citico darter, smoky madtom and yellowfin madtom - in a creek supporting about 100 native fish, 10 mussel and 12 crayfish species.
stories.notes: Lat/lon approximate - page describes a remote reach of Citico Creek near Indian Boundary in the Cherokee National Forest; county not stated on the page. Also documented at: https://www.americanrivers.org/2026/03/100-dams-down-2025-a-big-year-for-reconnecting-rivers-in-the-u-s/

stories.title: Spotfin Chub Restoration, Tellico River
stories.orgs: Conservation Fisheries Inc.; U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service; USDA Forest Service (Cherokee National Forest); Tennessee Wildlife Resources Agency
stories.desc: Conservation Fisheries began captive propagation and release of the threatened spotfin chub into the Tellico River in 2002 after the species had been lost from the drainage. The organization reports regular sightings of wild-reproducing spotfin chub in the Tellico, making it one of its established reintroduction successes. Propagation of the species has continued since 1994, with up to roughly 10,000 larvae produced in some years for release and monitoring across its range.
stories.notes: Coordinates approximate (lower-middle Tellico River).

stories.title: Cane Creek Livestock Exclusion and Stormwater Relocation, Etowah
stories.orgs: USDA Natural Resources Conservation Service; McMinn County Soil Conservation District; City of Etowah; Tennessee Department of Environment and Conservation; Tennessee Department of Agriculture
lpOrgs: Tennessee Department of Environment and Conservation
stories.desc: On Cane Creek near Etowah, partners installed 12 geotextile-and-gravel heavy-use areas (nine on a 400-acre farm and three on a smaller farm), fenced cattle out of the stream, built stabilized stream crossings where access was necessary, and planted trees in critical areas to reduce erosion and add habitat; the City of Etowah also relocated its stormwater discharge off Cane Creek. Fecal coliform readings fell to 640 colonies per 100 mL or fewer, below the 1,000-colony criterion that had caused the listing. Cane Creek was removed from Tennessee's 303(d) impaired waters list in 2004.
stories.notes: Coordinates approximate.

stories.title: Little Shoal Creek Grassed Waterways and Pasture Renovation
stories.orgs: USDA Natural Resources Conservation Service; Lawrence County Soil Conservation District; Tennessee Department of Agriculture; USEPA Section 319 program
stories.desc: Conservation tillage, cropland conversion, pasture renovation and hay planting were applied along Little Shoal Creek and its tributaries Crossfield Branch and Fourmile Hollow, including grassed waterways on 150 acres of farmland adjoining streams and legume seeding of bare ground. Taxa richness rose from 12 in 1999 to 28 in 2003 and the Biorecon score of 13 fell in the non-impaired range. The creek was removed from Tennessee's 303(d) list in 2004.
stories.sector: Partnership (federal, state, local district, private landowners)
stories.notes: Middle Tennessee. Lat/lon approximate; nearest town not stated in the source.

stories.title: Harms Mill Dam Removal, Elk River
stories.orgs: Tennessee Wildlife Resources Agency (project partner lead); U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service (National Fish Passage Program); Tennessee Wildlife Resources Agency; The Nature Conservancy; National Fish and Wildlife Foundation; Tennessee Valley Authority; Maddox Family Foundation; The Nature Conservancy in Tennessee
stories.desc: TWRA acquired the obsolete 1922 Fayetteville Light and Power concrete dam and powerhouse at the historic Harms Mill site in 2021; permits were finalized in 2024 and crews dismantled most of the structure within a week in October 2025. TNC calls it the largest dam removal of its kind in Tennessee, reconnecting roughly 1,114 miles of free-flowing river (804 downstream and 780 upstream miles had been separated). Fish and mussels, including the endangered boulder darter, were salvaged ahead of demolition; the Elk River supports 19 federally listed species.
stories.notes: South-Middle Tennessee, not East Tennessee; included because the slice covers Tennessee dam removals statewide. County inferred from Fayetteville; coordinates approximate. Project described on the same TNC dam-removal story page as Roaring River. Also documented at: https://www.fws.gov/project/harms-mill-dam-removal

stories.title: Lick Creek Cover Crops and Streambank Protection (Snake Creek watershed, McNairy County)
stories.orgs: McNairy County Soil Conservation District; Chickasaw-Shiloh Resource Conservation and Development Council; Tennessee Department of Agriculture; USEPA Section 319 program; private landowners
stories.desc: Landowners along a 20-mile reach of Lick Creek in the Snake Creek watershed planted pasture and hay cover crops to reduce cropland erosion and installed streambank protection to cut siltation and improve habitat, with practices mapped from 1999 through 2005. A 2004 biological reconnaissance survey scored 11, within the non-impaired range, and the creek met narrative criteria for turbidity and total suspended solids. The 20 miles were removed from the 2006 303(d) list.
stories.sector: Partnership (federal, state, local district, private landowners)
stories.notes: West Tennessee. Lat/lon approximate; nearest town not stated in the source.

stories.title: Gunpowder Creek stream restoration and siltation delisting
stories.orgs: Boone County Conservation District; cities of Florence and Union; Sanitation District No. 1; Northern Kentucky University Stream and Wetland Restoration Program; Kentucky Division of Water; Kentucky NRCS; U.S. EPA
stories.desc: Northern Kentucky University restored about 2,700 feet of eroding stream channel in Florence ($239,000), riparian buffers were widened with 2,000+ trees per acre, 14,800 linear feet of exclusion/rotational-grazing fence and BMPs on 10,000+ agricultural acres were installed, and stormwater basins were retrofitted including a bankfull stormwater wetland (2017). Macroinvertebrate scores improved from poor (1990s) to good (2014) and the 15-mile lower segment was delisted for siltation in the 2018/2020 Integrated Report.

Year-3 monitoring was completed December 2021 with a release request to follow.

stories.title: Minors Creek stream restoration (Kleber WMA)
stories.orgs: Kentucky Department of Fish and Wildlife Resources (Stream and Wetland Mitigation Fee-In-Lieu-Of Program)
lpOrgs: Kentucky Department of Fish and Wildlife Resources
stories.desc: On a 309-acre addition to the Kleber Wildlife Management Area in Owen County, KDFWR's mitigation program restored Minors Creek and its tributaries with construction from 2017 to 2019. Year-3 monitoring was reported in December 2021 with release to long-term management under discussion.
stories.notes: Location approximate.

stories.title: Fleming Creek agricultural BMPs and delistings
stories.orgs: Fleming County Conservation District; USDA NRCS; Kentucky Division of Conservation; Kentucky Division of Water; Redwing Ecological Services; University of Kentucky Cooperative Extension; Community Farm Alliance; landowners
stories.desc: Roughly $3.6 million in state, federal and landowner investment since 1991 installed about 80 animal waste facilities, roughly 30 miles of riparian/exclusion fencing (54,700 ft livestock-exclusion and 39,352 ft rotational-grazing fence under the 2004 grant alone), 200+ alternative watering facilities and heavy-use pads across the Allison Creek, Wilson Run and Stockton Creek subwatersheds. A 4.8-mile segment was delisted for aquatic life in 2006 (macroinvertebrate score 68.5, 'good'), and a 12.8-mile segment (RM 0.0-12.8) was delisted for nutrient impairment in the 2024 Integrated Report.
stories.notes: 2024 delisting detail from KY NPS Annual Report 2025: https://eec.ky.gov/Environmental-Protection/Water/Protection/ArchivedNPSDocs/KYNPSAnnualReport2025.pdf

stories.title: South Fork Currys Fork stream and wetland restoration

lpOrgs: Kentucky Department of Fish and Wildlife Resources
stories.desc: KDFWR restored 4,638 linear feet of South Fork Currys Fork plus 1.33 acres of wetland in Oldham County in 2012, part of the upstream work credited with reducing sediment to Floyds Fork; the site was inspected in January 2022 with no issues.

stories.title: Rogers Gap / Veterans Memorial WMA stream restoration
stories.orgs: Kentucky Department of Fish and Wildlife Resources (Stream and Wetland Mitigation Fee-In-Lieu-Of Program); Stantec (design-build)
lpOrgs: Kentucky Department of Fish and Wildlife Resources
stories.desc: On the 2,500-acre Veterans Memorial Wildlife Management Area near Sadieville, a 2013 design-build contract restored and protected roughly 28 miles of stream channel and riparian corridor, with construction completed in 2016. Year-5 monitoring (2021) followed supplemental planting of about 15,500 live stakes and 300+ trees in 2020; a release request to long-term management was planned.

stories.title: Myers Station stream restoration (Clay WMA)
stories.orgs: Kentucky Department of Fish and Wildlife Resources (Stream and Wetland Mitigation Fee-In-Lieu-Of Program)
lpOrgs: Kentucky Department of Fish and Wildlife Resources
stories.desc: On 462 acres added to the Clay Wildlife Management Area in Nicholas County, KDFWR restored Coon Creek, Cassidy Creek and tributaries in the Lower Licking basin. Year-5 monitoring (2021) found the north side meeting success criteria with partial release pending, while the south side needed remedial work.
stories.notes: Construction year inferred from Year-5 monitoring in 2021.

stories.title: Floyds Fork / Currys Fork sediment delisting
stories.orgs: Kentucky Division of Water; USDA NRCS; Kentucky Division of Conservation; Oldham County Fiscal Court; Kentucky Department of Fish and Wildlife Resources; Currys Fork Watershed Association; Kentucky Waterways Alliance; Floyds Fork Environmental Association; University of Louisville Stream Institute
lpOrgs: Kentucky Department of Fish and Wildlife Resources
stories.desc: Upstream in the Currys Fork watershed partners restored more than 3,700 linear feet of stream channel (KDFWR in-lieu-fee funded, $878,000), established 1,695 acres of riparian forest buffer and 1,020 ft of vegetative buffer, cutting sediment delivery by 239.7 tons/yr, while 1,217 agricultural BMPs were installed across six upstream watersheds. Macroinvertebrate scores rose from fair (1999) to excellent (76.6) and fish IBI to 'good' by 2012, and the 9.9-mile Floyds Fork segment (RM 24.2-34.1) was delisted for siltation in 2016.

stories.title: Townsend Creek livestock exclusion and riparian restoration
stories.orgs: The Nature Conservancy (Kentucky Chapter); Kentucky Division of Water; USDA NRCS; USDA Farm Service Agency; Bourbon and Harrison county conservation districts; Kentucky Department of Fish and Wildlife Resources (in-lieu-fee match); landowners
lpOrgs: Kentucky Department of Fish and Wildlife Resources
stories.desc: Using a 2003 $1.5 million 319 grant (about $435,000 for on-the-ground work) TNC and partners installed stream crossings, livestock exclusion fencing, riparian forest and grass buffers, sinkhole protection, waste storage, alternative watering, shade structures and wetland easements across the 25,648-acre South Fork Licking tributary in 2003-2005. Fecal coliform exceedances dropped to 12 percent of samples and miles 0.0-2.9 were delisted in 2012.

stories.title: Elkhorn Dam Removal, Elkhorn Creek
stories.orgs: Listed in American Rivers' national dam removal inventory; removing parties not named in the source
stories.desc: The Elkhorn Dam was removed from Elkhorn Creek in Franklin County in 2021, restoring free flow on one of Kentucky's best-known smallmouth bass and paddling streams just above its confluence with the Kentucky River. The annual report records the removal but does not report height, reconnected mileage or partners.
stories.notes: Record derived from Table 1 of American Rivers' 2021 report (PDF verified). Lat/lon approximate.

stories.title: Big Farm stream and wetland restoration (Clay WMA)

lpOrgs: Kentucky Department of Fish and Wildlife Resources
stories.desc: On a 490-acre Clay WMA tract in Bath County, KDFWR constructed stream and wetland restoration in 2020; flood damage repairs and riparian planting were completed in late 2021 and Year-1 monitoring began in 2022.
stories.notes: Location approximate.

stories.title: Cove Spring stream and wetland restoration (Frankfort)
stories.orgs: Kentucky Department of Fish and Wildlife Resources (Stream and Wetland Mitigation Fee-In-Lieu-Of Program); City of Frankfort (Cove Spring Park)
lpOrgs: Kentucky Department of Fish and Wildlife Resources
stories.desc: At Cove Spring Park in Frankfort, KDFWR restored 7,203 linear feet of stream and 20.92 acres of wetland, completed in 2013, using natural channel design and native plantings. The site is in long-term management; a 2021 inspection noted tree cutting and riparian discharge by the state highway cabinet that was being resolved.

stories.title: Stoner Creek E. coli delisting (Hancock Creek initiative)
stories.orgs: USDA NRCS; Kentucky Division of Conservation; Friends of Stoner Creek; Strodes Creek Conservancy; Kentucky Division of Water; local producers
stories.desc: NRCS installed 112 BMPs in the Stoner Creek headwaters and 90 in Strodes Creek (riparian forest buffers, critical area planting, heavy-use areas, watering facilities), a rotational grazing system and feeding pads were built, and the 2010-2013 Hancock Creek Watershed Improvement Initiative added riparian buffer zones, tree plantings and rain gardens. The geometric mean fell below the 130 col/100 mL standard and the 6.6-mile segment (RM 23.5-30.1) was delisted for E. coli in the 2016 Integrated Report.

stories.title: East Fork Little Sandy River stream restoration
stories.orgs: Kentucky Department of Fish and Wildlife Resources (Stream and Wetland Mitigation Fee-In-Lieu-Of Program)
lpOrgs: Kentucky Department of Fish and Wildlife Resources
stories.desc: Four contiguous KDFWR mitigation projects on the East Fork Little Sandy River in Lawrence County restored a combined 21,187 linear feet (1,522; 9,000; 7,496; 3,169 ft) of eroding channel in 2010-2011 using natural channel design, bank grading and riparian planting. Before-and-after photos are shown on the program page; 2021 inspections found no instability.

stories.title: Salt Lick Creek stream restoration (Bath County)
stories.orgs: Kentucky Department of Fish and Wildlife Resources (Stream and Wetland Mitigation Fee-In-Lieu-Of Program)
lpOrgs: Kentucky Department of Fish and Wildlife Resources
stories.desc: KDFWR's mitigation program restored eroding reaches of Salt Lick Creek in Bath County; construction photos appear on the program page and the 2021 annual report lists a follow-up repair planned for summer 2022.
stories.notes: Construction year not stated in sources.

stories.title: Slabcamp / Stonecoal Creek stream restoration (Daniel Boone NF)
stories.orgs: Kentucky Department of Fish and Wildlife Resources (Stream and Wetland Mitigation Fee-In-Lieu-Of Program); U.S. Forest Service - Daniel Boone National Forest
lpOrgs: Kentucky Department of Fish and Wildlife Resources
stories.desc: In Rowan County, 48,819 linear feet (about 9 miles) of Slabcamp and Stonecoal creeks, tributaries of the Licking River within the Daniel Boone National Forest, were restored and protected under KDFWR's mitigation program, completed in 2013 and released to long-term management. 2021 inspection found no instability or easement violations.

stories.title: Wolf Run Regency Road detention basin retrofit (Lexington)
stories.orgs: Lexington-Fayette Urban County Government; Kentucky Division of Water (319(h)); Friends of Wolf Run
stories.desc: In the urban Wolf Run watershed in Lexington, 319(h) funds were used to retrofit the Regency Road stormwater detention basins: concrete channels were removed, wetland micropools installed and trees planted to treat runoff and restore more natural hydrology ahead of the impaired stream.
stories.notes: Urban stormwater wetland retrofit; a second (Southland) basin was designed but not built as of the report.

stories.title: East Fork Indian Creek stream restoration (Daniel Boone NF)
stories.orgs: Kentucky Department of Fish and Wildlife Resources (Stream and Wetland Mitigation Fee-In-Lieu-Of Program); U.S. Forest Service - Daniel Boone National Forest
lpOrgs: Kentucky Department of Fish and Wildlife Resources
stories.desc: KDFWR restored East Fork Indian Creek on Daniel Boone National Forest land in Menifee County near Red River Gorge; Year-5 monitoring was reported December 2020, repairs completed December 2021 and final planting in early 2022 ahead of release.
stories.notes: Construction year inferred from Year-5 monitoring in 2020.

stories.title: Mill Creek Elementary stream restoration (Lexington)
stories.orgs: Kentucky Department of Fish and Wildlife Resources (Stream and Wetland Mitigation Fee-In-Lieu-Of Program); Fayette County Public Schools
lpOrgs: Kentucky Department of Fish and Wildlife Resources
stories.desc: An urban demonstration project restored 680 linear feet of a degraded stream on the Mill Creek Elementary School grounds in Lexington in 2009, creating an outdoor classroom; inspected January 2022 with no issues.

stories.title: Sulphur Creek watershed livestock exclusion (Salt River basin)
stories.orgs: Anderson County Conservation District; Mercer County Health Department; Kentucky Division of Water; USDA NRCS
stories.desc: More than $769,000 in 319(h) funds supported 33,470 feet of stream-exclusion fencing, 6,118 ft of livestock pipeline, 46 alternative water sources, 220 acres of heavy-use protection, feedlot relocation and pasture plantings (including 15,034 ft of fence and 9 feed pads in the Cheese Lick subwatershed) plus 26 septic repairs. E. coli geometric means fell from 230-244 MPN (2012-13) to 69-86 MPN (2023); the stream remains listed pending single-sample compliance and a TMDL Alternative was issued in 2023.
stories.notes: Not yet delisted; water-quality improvement documented.

stories.title: West Hickman Creek low-head dam removal
stories.orgs: Kentucky Division of Water; West Hickman Creek watershed partners
stories.desc: As part of implementing the EPA-accepted West Hickman Creek watershed plan south of Lexington, a non-functioning low-head dam in the lower watershed was removed, restoring stream continuity. Reported in the Kentucky 2025 Nonpoint Source annual report.
stories.notes: Thin detail in source (one-line mention); location approximate.

stories.title: Yellowbank Creek nutrient and sediment delisting
stories.orgs: Kentucky Department of Agriculture; USGS Kentucky Water Science Center; USDA NRCS; UK Cooperative Extension; Breckinridge and Meade county conservation districts; Kentucky Division of Forestry; KDFWR; Kentucky Corn Growers Association; Kentucky Division of Water
lpOrgs: Kentucky Department of Fish and Wildlife Resources
stories.desc: After a $535,000 319(h) grant funded demonstration farms and three field days (221 attendees), NRCS reported 87 practices installed in the watershed since 2005 - stream fencing, prescribed grazing, watering facilities, heavy-use protection, grassed waterways, contour farming and pesticide setbacks/stream buffers. A 2009 fish-community score of 'good' supported warmwater aquatic habitat use and the 10.3-mile Ohio River tributary was delisted for nutrients and sediment in 2012.

stories.title: City of Vine Grove Weir Dam Removal, Brushy Fork

stories.desc: A municipal weir dam was removed from Brushy Fork at Vine Grove in 2023, restoring free-flowing conditions and aquatic organism passage on this Salt River basin stream. The annual summary records the removal but does not report height, reconnected mileage or additional partners.

stories.title: Eagle Creek tributary wetland restoration (Higginson-Henry WMA)

stories.title: Red Lick Creek stream restoration

lpOrgs: Kentucky Department of Fish and Wildlife Resources

A 2021 inspection noted 100-150 ft of right-bank erosion near a bridge where a water district cleared vegetation.
stories.notes: Location approximate.

stories.title: Ross Creek stream restoration (Lee / Estill counties)

stories.title: Dix River / Hanging Fork livestock exclusion and delisting

stories.title: Goose Creek stream restoration (Casey County)

stories.title: Roundstone Creek Dam Removal

stories.desc: A dam on Roundstone Creek at Mount Vernon was removed in 2023, restoring free flow and aquatic organism passage in this Rockcastle River headwater stream in the Cumberland basin. The annual summary records the removal but does not give height, mileage or partners.

stories.title: Terry's Branch and Balls Fork stream restoration (Knott County)

stories.title: Green River riparian protection and hardwood planting, Hart County
stories.orgs: The Nature Conservancy
stories.desc: In 2015 TNC permanently protected 200 acres of high-priority riparian land on the Green River in Hart County, covering three miles of river and stream frontage, and planted more than 100,000 native hardwood trees on the property to shade and buffer the river upstream of Mammoth Cave.
stories.notes: Exact tract location not given; coordinates near Munfordville.

stories.title: Green River Lake Dam environmental flow restoration (Sustainable Rivers Program)
stories.orgs: The Nature Conservancy; U.S. Army Corps of Engineers
stories.desc: The first Sustainable Rivers Program site in the nation: beginning in the early 2000s the Corps changed Green River Lake Dam operations to use multiple outlets (warming cold bottom releases) and delayed the fall drawdown so downstream flows mimic natural patterns. Shortly afterward researchers began finding juvenile mussels downstream for the first time, and the approach has been replicated on dozens of Corps reservoirs.
stories.water: Green River below Green River Lake
stories.notes: Hydrologic (flow) restoration rather than structural work; type is best fit.

stories.title: Bullskin Creek stream restoration

lpOrgs: Kentucky Department of Fish and Wildlife Resources

stories.notes: Location approximate.

stories.title: Green River Lock and Dam No. 6 Removal
stories.orgs: The Nature Conservancy; U.S. Army Corps of Engineers; U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service; Kentucky Department of Fish and Wildlife Resources; U.S. Army Corps of Engineers Louisville District; U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service (National Fish Passage Program); Kentucky Waterways Alliance; Mammoth Cave National Park (NPS); Edmonson County Water District; The Nature Conservancy in Kentucky; US Army Corps of Engineers; US Fish and Wildlife Service; Barren River Area Development District; Green River Blueway; Mammoth Cave National Park
lpOrgs: Kentucky Department of Fish and Wildlife Resources
stories.desc: Lock and Dam No. 6, a 1900s navigation structure on the Green River near Mammoth Cave National Park, developed seepage and cracking and breached in November 2016; removal was completed in March 2017. Taking the dam out restored free-flowing conditions and eliminated a bank-erosion threat to a drinking water intake a half mile downstream in Edmonson County. The Green River supports more than 150 fish species and 70 mussel species, and surveys found sportfish in free-flowing reaches healthier and more numerous than in the impounded pools.
stories.notes: Coordinates approximate (Green River at Brownsville / Mammoth Cave reach). Also documented at: https://www.nature.org/en-us/about-us/where-we-work/united-states/kentucky/stories-in-kentucky/profile-of-the-green-river/; https://www.americanrivers.org/wp-content/uploads/2023/02/DamList2022_Summary_02132023.pdf; https://www.fws.gov/story/2021-07/going-going; https://www.americanrivers.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/DamList2024_Summary_03032025_Revised.pdf

stories.title: North Fork Kentucky River bank stabilization (SECC, Whitesburg)
stories.orgs: Kentucky Department of Fish and Wildlife Resources (Stream and Wetland Mitigation Fee-In-Lieu-Of Program); Southeast Kentucky Community and Technical College
lpOrgs: Kentucky Department of Fish and Wildlife Resources
stories.desc: KDFWR stabilized 825 linear feet of the North Fork Kentucky River bank at the Southeast Kentucky Community College campus in Whitesburg in 2006 using natural channel techniques; before-and-after photos are on the program page and the reach was stable in 2021.

stories.title: Buck Creek - Pumphrey Tract stream restoration
stories.orgs: Kentucky Department of Fish and Wildlife Resources (Stream and Wetland Mitigation Fee-In-Lieu-Of Program); The Nature Conservancy
lpOrgs: Kentucky Department of Fish and Wildlife Resources
stories.desc: KDFWR's in-lieu-fee program restored and protected 62,345 linear feet (nearly 12 miles) of Buck Creek and tributaries on the TNC-protected Pumphrey Tract in Pulaski County, completed in 2009. The reach supports a diverse Cumberland River mussel fauna; 2021 long-term management inspection found no easement violations or channel instability.

stories.title: Elisha Creek stream restoration (Daniel Boone NF, Redbird District)
stories.orgs: Kentucky Department of Fish and Wildlife Resources (Stream and Wetland Mitigation Fee-In-Lieu-Of Program); U.S. Forest Service - Daniel Boone National Forest
lpOrgs: Kentucky Department of Fish and Wildlife Resources
stories.desc: KDFWR restored 4,227 linear feet of Elisha Creek on Forest Service land in Leslie County in the Red Bird River watershed, completed in 2013 and now protected by the USFS; 2021 inspection found no instability.
stories.notes: Location approximate.

stories.title: Red Bird River watershed restoration and E. coli delisting
stories.orgs: U.S. Forest Service - Daniel Boone National Forest; Kentucky Division of Water; Red Bird Mission; Eastern Kentucky PRIDE; University of Kentucky; Cumberland Valley RC&D Council; Red Bird River Watershed Team
stories.desc: With $409,000 in 319(h) grants to the Daniel Boone National Forest (2015, 2019), partners replaced or installed 30 failing septic systems and pumped out 24 more, volunteers cleaned 16.6 miles of stream, and erosion was mitigated along 69.2 miles of forest trails draining to the river. All 2018 recreation-season samples were below the delisting threshold and the 15.35-mile lower Red Bird River was delisted for E. coli in the 2022 Integrated Report.
stories.notes: On-the-ground work is septic replacement plus trail erosion control and cleanups rather than channel work.

stories.title: Crane's Nest stream and wetland restoration
stories.orgs: Kentucky Department of Fish and Wildlife Resources (Stream and Wetland Mitigation Fee-In-Lieu-Of Program)
lpOrgs: Kentucky Department of Fish and Wildlife Resources
stories.desc: KDFWR restored 2,253 linear feet of stream and 4 acres of wetland at the Crane's Nest site in Knox County (Upper Cumberland) in 2013; the site is in long-term management with no violations noted in 2021.
stories.notes: Location approximate.

stories.title: Hatchery Creek constructed trout stream (Wolf Creek National Fish Hatchery)
stories.orgs: Kentucky Department of Fish and Wildlife Resources (Stream and Wetland Mitigation Fee-In-Lieu-Of Program); U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service Wolf Creek National Fish Hatchery; U.S. Army Corps of Engineers; Stantec
lpOrgs: Kentucky Department of Fish and Wildlife Resources
stories.desc: Below Wolf Creek Dam the short hatchery outflow was replaced with a newly constructed, roughly one-mile natural-channel stream with pools, riffles, spawning gravel and large wood, built from August 2014 to early 2016 with in-lieu-fee mitigation funds. The stream now supports a popular year-round trout fishery with documented natural trout reproduction; Year-5 monitoring was completed in 2020 and the site is in compliance review for release.
stories.notes: Stream length and trout reproduction from general knowledge of the project; report confirms construction dates and monitoring.

stories.title: Clarks River E. coli delisting
stories.orgs: U.S. EPA; Kentucky Division of Water; Jackson Purchase Foundation; Marshall County Fiscal Court; City of Murray; Kentucky NRCS; Kentucky Division of Conservation
stories.desc: NRCS installed 2,521 agricultural practices on nearly 40,000 acres (riparian buffers, stream exclusion fencing, cover crops) in 2008-2015, 40 septic systems were repaired, a community lagoon replaced 40 failing septics, and sewer was extended to about 100 homes. By 2015 the 7.5-mile Clarks River segment (RM 13.1-20.55) met E. coli criteria and was proposed for delisting in the 2018/2020 Integrated Report.

stories.title: Trammel Creek stream restoration (Allen County)
stories.orgs: Kentucky Department of Fish and Wildlife Resources (Stream and Wetland Mitigation Fee-In-Lieu-Of Program)
lpOrgs: Kentucky Department of Fish and Wildlife Resources
stories.desc: KDFWR restored Trammel Creek, a Barren River tributary near Scottsville, under its mitigation program; a Year-8 monitoring report was submitted by 2021 and repairs began in early 2022 ahead of release to long-term management.
stories.notes: Construction year inferred from Year-8 monitoring.

stories.title: Bayou de Chien / Cane Creek watershed delisting
stories.orgs: USDA NRCS; Jackson Purchase RC&D Foundation; Four Rivers Watershed Basin Team; Kentucky Division of Water
stories.desc: Beginning in 2006 more than 361 agricultural BMPs - livestock waste storage, grassed filter strips and waterways, grazing management and livestock stream-access control, wetland restoration, cover crops and no-till - were installed in the Cane Creek tributary watershed. Monitoring 2007-2010 showed the 5.5-mile Bayou de Chien segment (RM 8.8-14.3) met bacteria standards, and it was delisted for fecal coliform in Kentucky's 2012 Integrated Report.

stories.title: Obion Creek wetland restoration (Hickman County)
stories.orgs: Kentucky Department of Fish and Wildlife Resources (Stream and Wetland Mitigation Fee-In-Lieu-Of Program)
lpOrgs: Kentucky Department of Fish and Wildlife Resources
stories.desc: KDFWR's mitigation program restored bottomland wetlands along Obion Creek in Hickman County in two phases; Obion Creek 1 has been released to long-term management and Obion Creek 2 reached Year-5 monitoring in 2021 with additional invasive-species treatment planned.
stories.notes: Location approximate.

stories.title: Rock Creek acid mine drainage remediation (Big South Fork)
stories.orgs: Kentucky Division of Abandoned Mine Lands; Rock Creek Task Force (12 state/federal agencies and conservation groups incl. USGS, NOAA, U.S. Forest Service, Office of Surface Mining)
stories.desc: Phase 1 (spring 2000, $970,000) removed 25,000 cubic yards of coal refuse from streamside areas along a 4-mile reach with 40+ mine portals, built open limestone channels and a vertical-flow treatment wetland, revegetated banks and began monthly limestone-sand dosing. Acid loading to the Big South Fork Cumberland fell from 110 metric tons/month to near zero, sediment delivery dropped 500 tons/yr, and fish returned to stations that previously had none; the stream moved from non-support to partial support on the 2002 303(d) list.

stories.title: Western Kentucky floodplain wetland restoration (TNC / NRCS Wetland Reserve)
stories.orgs: The Nature Conservancy; USDA Natural Resources Conservation Service; Murray State University; Tennessee Tech University
stories.desc: Since 2011 TNC and NRCS have enrolled more than 19,000 acres of frequently flooded cropland across an eight-county area of western Kentucky in wetland easements, replanting cypress and bottomland oaks at 435 seedlings per acre and plugging drainage ditches or installing water-control structures to restore hydrology. A $4.36 million six-year monitoring study (2018-2024) found restored sites retain nutrients and filter water better than unrestored land and support abundant wildlife.
stories.notes: Multi-site program; coordinates at the Obion Creek-Mississippi confluence area of the Big Rivers Corridor.

stories.title: Riparian Buffer Establishment at Walls of Jericho and Henshaw Cove, Paint Rock Headwaters
stories.orgs: Alabama Department of Conservation and Natural Resources (State Wildlife Grant); Forever Wild Land Trust; The Nature Conservancy; U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service
stories.desc: A 2009-2011 State Wildlife Grant project reforested riparian buffers and enhanced wildlife habitat on the Walls of Jericho and Henshaw Cove tracts in the headwaters of the Paint Rock River, protecting water quality for the watershed's rare mussels and snails. The project was one of the early habitat actions supporting the Paint Rock's listed mussel recovery.
stories.water: Hurricane Creek / Paint Rock River headwaters
stories.notes: Only a project listing (title, dates, location) is published; acreage and outcomes not reported. Coordinates approximate (Walls of Jericho tract).

stories.title: Hester Creek stream stabilization and riparian buffers (Flint River watershed)
stories.orgs: Madison County SWCD; ADEM; Alabama A&M University; Flint River Conservation Association; City of Huntsville; Huntsville Utilities; TVA; Tennessee River Basin Clean Water Partnership; USDA NRCS; USGS; USFWS; USDA FSA; Land Trust of North Alabama; TARCOG; farmers
stories.desc: Four Section 319 grants (about $496K federal, $489K match) between 2000 and 2013 funded roughly 12,500 feet of stream channel stabilization and 14 acres of riparian buffer on the 7.27-mile Hester Creek, plus livestock crossings, fencing, alternative water, rotational grazing, cover crops, terraces and cropland conversion; Madison County adopted stormwater ordinances in 2005. ADEM delisted the creek in 2012 for nutrients and turbidity, with fish and macroinvertebrate communities rated fair.
stories.town: Hazel Green / New Market (NE of Huntsville)

stories.title: Paint Rock River Streambank Restoration and Mussel Recovery at the Jones Property
stories.orgs: Alabama Department of Conservation and Natural Resources / Alabama Aquatic Biodiversity Center; U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service Partners for Fish and Wildlife; The Nature Conservancy in Alabama; Alabama Rivers Alliance; Beagle Charitable Foundation; Tennessee Valley Authority; Jackson County; USDA NRCS; Tennessee Wildlife Resources Agency; Jones family (private landowners)
stories.desc: On a ~5,000-acre private farm where the Paint Rock River meanders about 3 miles (channelized by the Corps in the 1960s and heavily eroding), partners began restoration in 2012 and completed major streambank stabilization projects in 2017 and 2019. Since 2010 the Alabama Aquatic Biodiversity Center has released more than 23,000 propagated mussels at this site (53,000 of six species river-wide), including ~1,500 pale lilliput, Tennessee bean and Cumberland moccasinshell in August 2026; natural reproduction has been confirmed for pale lilliput, birdwing pearlymussel, oystermussel and Alabama lampmussel in the middle and lower river.
stories.notes: Property is in rural Jackson County on the middle Paint Rock; exact location not published, coordinates approximate.

stories.title: Roy B. Whitaker Preserve Floodplain and Cole Springs Branch Restoration
stories.orgs: The Nature Conservancy in Alabama; local landowners and community
stories.desc: After acquiring this 323-acre former cattle pasture on 1.5 miles of the Paint Rock River in 2005, TNC returned Cole Springs Branch to its original channel, replanted floodplain hardwood forest and native warm-season grasses, removed low-water stream crossings and restored streambanks, and manages the site with prescribed fire and invasive plant control. The preserve now supports returning wildlife including bald eagles and great blue herons and is a stop on the North Alabama Birding Trail.
stories.water: Paint Rock River / Cole Springs Branch
stories.notes: Coordinates from TNC's preserve map. Acreage restored and quantitative outcomes not published.

stories.title: Paint Rock River Mainstem Bioengineered Streambank Restoration (350 ft)
stories.orgs: The Nature Conservancy in Alabama; U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service Partners for Fish and Wildlife; Geological Survey of Alabama; USDA NRCS Regional Conservation Partnership Program; Tennessee Valley Authority; Alabama Rivers and Streams Network; Alabama Aquatic Biodiversity Center
stories.desc: In 2026 TNC and Alabama Rivers and Streams Network partners completed another streambank restoration on the mainstem Paint Rock River, treating about 350 linear feet of eroding bank with nature-based bioengineering that combined woody debris structures and native sod transplants. Pre-project surveys found more than 20 mussel species (several state and federally listed); the project is expected to keep an estimated 150 metric tons of sediment out of the river annually, and the restored reaches are being used by the Alabama Aquatic Biodiversity Center as reintroduction sites for imperiled mussels.
stories.notes: Described in the Oct 22, 2026 item on TNC's Alabama Conservation News page (no standalone URL). Part of TNC's 5-year NRCS RCPP Streambank Restoration Initiative (see https://www.nature.org/en-us/about-us/where-we-work/united-states/alabama/stories-in-alabama/protecting-farmland-water/). Exact site not published; coordinates approximate.

stories.title: Paint Rock River Initiative: 45 Streambank and Channel Restoration Projects
stories.orgs: The Nature Conservancy (Alabama Chapter); U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service Partners for Fish and Wildlife; USDA NRCS; Alabama Department of Conservation and Natural Resources; private landowners
stories.desc: Launched by TNC's Alabama Chapter in 1994 to repair erosion caused by 1960s Corps channelization of the upper Paint Rock, the Paint Rock River Initiative completed 45 streambank and channel restoration projects on private farms over roughly two decades, using natural channel design, bank re-grading, rock and wood structures and tree plantings. The work reduced sediment loads in a river that supports nearly 100 native fish and 52 mussel species (12 federally listed) and set the stage for the mussel reintroductions now reproducing in the middle and lower river.
stories.notes: Project count and dates come from the ADCNR article https://www.outdooralabama.com/articles/it-takes-village-clean-river-habitat-restoration-and-mussel-recovery-paint-rock; the TNC link describes the bank-stabilization program generally. Watershed-scale entry; coordinates are the mid-watershed.

stories.title: Paint Rock River streambank stabilization program (TNC Streambank Restoration Initiative)
stories.orgs: The Nature Conservancy; USDA NRCS (RCPP); USFWS Partners for Fish and Wildlife; Geological Survey of Alabama; ADEM; ADCNR; private landowners
stories.desc: TNC's Alabama freshwater team has completed more than 40 bank stabilization and sediment-abatement projects on farms in the Paint Rock River watershed using natural channel design, toe wood and rock, tree plantings and livestock fencing, expanded since 2021 through a $1M NRCS RCPP award covering the Paint Rock, Locust Fork and Big Canoe Creek watersheds. The most recent project (October 2026) stabilized about 350 feet of eroding bank with natural materials, expected to keep roughly 150 metric tons of sediment a year out of this mussel- and fish-rich river.
stories.notes: Program-level entry; individual site locations not published. Supporting docs: https://www.nature.org/content/dam/tnc/nature/en/documents/alabama-case-for-support.pdf and https://www.nature.org/en-us/about-us/where-we-work/united-states/alabama/stories-in-alabama/protecting-farmland-water/

stories.title: Cumberland Moccasinshell Reintroduction in Bear Creek
stories.orgs: Alabama Aquatic Biodiversity Center (ADCNR); U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service; Tennessee Valley Authority
stories.desc: The Alabama Aquatic Biodiversity Center reintroduced propagated Cumberland moccasinshell mussels (proposed for federal listing and surviving at only two Alabama sites) into Bear Creek in Colbert County as part of its Tennessee River basin mussel recovery program. ADCNR reports the reintroduced Bear Creek population is now reproducing, one of the first self-sustaining reintroductions of this species.
stories.notes: Mentioned briefly within the Paint Rock article; release years and numbers not published. Coordinates approximate for Bear Creek in Colbert County. Photo is from the Paint Rock release, not Bear Creek.

stories.title: Lower Flint River livestock BMPs and organic enrichment delisting
stories.orgs: ADEM; Madison County SWCD; USDA NRCS; Tennessee Valley Authority; Flint River Conservation Association; City of Huntsville; local landowners
stories.desc: Between 2001 and 2003 the Flint River watershed project ($250K Section 319 plus $331K match) put winter cover and conservation tillage on 2,000 acres, installed stream crossings, alternative watering, exclusion fencing and rotational grazing on 10 farms (400 acres), built 13 heavy-use areas and wrote nutrient plans for 300 acres. Dissolved oxygen monitoring in 2003 and 2005 supported removal of the 28-mile lower mainstem from the 2006 303(d) list for organic enrichment/low DO.
stories.notes: Coordinates approximate for the lower mainstem.

stories.title: Little Paint Rock Creek riparian and livestock BMPs (Paint Rock River watershed)
stories.orgs: ADEM; Marshall County SWCD; USDA NRCS; Alabama Water Watch; Auburn University / Alabama Cooperative Extension System; Alabama Clean Water Partnership; Paint Rock River Watershed Conservancy District; Tennessee Valley RC&D; The Nature Conservancy; US EPA
stories.desc: Section 319 projects from 1994 to 2014 on the 5.88-mile Little Paint Rock Creek (13.1 sq mi) established riparian buffers, livestock management to keep cattle out of the stream, hydroseeding of disturbed soils, poultry waste and septic improvements and nutrient management plans. Monitoring from 1999 to 2021 showed CBOD and ammonia mostly below detection and ADEM concluded in its 2025 NPS annual report that the organic enrichment/low DO impairment on the 2.17-mile listed reach no longer exists.
stories.water: Little Paint Rock Creek (Short Creek / Guntersville Lake)
stories.sector: Partnership (SWCD, NRCS, state, extension, private landowners)
stories.notes: Source is ADEM's Alabama NPS Management Program Annual Report (success story section); coordinates approximate.

stories.title: Crowdabout Creek riparian forest buffers and livestock BMPs (Flint Creek watershed)
stories.orgs: Flint Creek Watershed Conservancy District; US EPA; ADEM; USDA NRCS; USDA FSA; Morgan County SWCD; Alabama Cooperative Extension System; Morgan County Commission; Tennessee Basin Clean Water Partnership; Alabama Mountains Rivers and Valleys RC&D; local farmers
stories.desc: From 2003 to 2009 farmers in the 31,150-acre Crowdabout Creek watershed planted 1,372 acres of riparian forest buffer, 132 acres of grassed waterways and about 90 acres of hardwoods, and installed exclusion fencing, cross-fencing and cattle stream crossings, with 1,594 acres enrolled in CRP. Minimum dissolved oxygen rose from 0.7 mg/L (1996) to 6.0 mg/L (2009), habitat improved from poor to fair, and by 2014 the 15-mile creek was listed as attaining standards for nutrients, siltation and CBOD; modeled reductions were 3,035 lb N, 3,537 lb P and 344 tons sediment per year.
stories.sector: Partnership (conservancy district, NRCS, state, private landowners)

stories.title: Scarham Creek NWQI livestock fencing and pasture BMPs (Guntersville Lake watershed)
stories.orgs: ADEM; DeKalb County SWCD; USDA NRCS; Top of Alabama Regional Council of Governments; local landowners
stories.desc: Two Section 319 projects (2002-2007, 2015-2018; $585K) and NRCS National Water Quality Initiative funding (2012-2022) installed about 55,000 feet of livestock fencing, 22,000 feet of livestock pipeline, 35 watering facilities, 31 waste storage facilities, 43 acres of stream access control, 2,520 acres of prescribed grazing and 3,300 acres of nutrient management on the 23.4-mile Scarham Creek. By 2022 ADEM found the organic enrichment/low DO and ammonia impairments no longer existed; pathogen, siltation and pesticide listings remain.

stories.title: Bear Creek watershed erosion-control BMPs and aluminum delisting
stories.orgs: Colbert, Franklin, Marion and Winston County SWCDs; Tennessee Valley Authority; USDA NRCS; ADEM; Bear Creek Outdoor Environmental Education Center; Alabama Water Watch; Alabama Cooperative Extension System; Alabama Cattlemen's Association; Alabama Dept. of Industrial Relations
stories.desc: From 2000 to 2005 partners installed filter strips, streambank protection, livestock exclusion fencing and restored abandoned surface-mine land across the 119-square-mile Bear Creek watershed (Tennessee River basin) with $337K in Section 319 funds and $376K in match. Erosion control cut soil-bound aluminum loading; sampling in 2009 and 2012 showed median aluminum below the ecoregional reference and ADEM delisted the 3-mile impaired segment in 2014.
stories.notes: Impaired segment is at the base of the watershed in Marion County; coordinates approximate.

stories.title: Unnamed Dam Removal, Big Wills Creek
stories.orgs: Listed in American Rivers' national dam removal inventory; removing parties not named in the source
stories.desc: An unnamed dam was removed from Big Wills Creek in Etowah County in 2022, restoring free flow on a Coosa River tributary in a basin known for high aquatic endemism. The national annual summary records the removal but does not report height, reconnected mileage or partner organizations.
stories.notes: Record derived from the 2022 dam removal summary table (PDF verified), which lists only 'Etowah' as the location. Lat/lon approximate.

stories.title: Dry Creek livestock exclusion, stream stabilization and delisting (Locust Fork watershed)
stories.orgs: Blount County SWCD; USDA NRCS; ADEM; US EPA; Alabama Dept. of Public Health; Cawaco RC&D; Alabama Water Watch; local landowners
stories.desc: Two Section 319 phases (2007-2010 and 2011-2014) on the 12-mile Dry Creek installed 47,766 ft of livestock fencing, 5 alternative water sources, 4,117 sq ft of livestock stream crossings, 210 ft of stream channel stabilization, heavy-use area protection, 32 acres of forage planting, alum treatment of poultry litter and 145 septic pump-outs. Ammonia impairment was delisted in 2012 and the nutrient and organic enrichment/DO impairments were removed in 2016; a pathogen listing remains.
stories.water: Dry Creek (Locust Fork, Black Warrior River)
stories.notes: Original 2015 EPA story: https://www.epa.gov/sites/default/files/2015-10/documents/al_drycreek.pdf

stories.title: Plicate Rocksnail Reintroduction in the Locust Fork of the Black Warrior River
stories.orgs: Alabama Aquatic Biodiversity Center (ADCNR Wildlife & Freshwater Fisheries); U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service; State Wildlife Grant Program
stories.desc: The Alabama Aquatic Biodiversity Center in Marion developed captive culture for the federally endangered plicate rocksnail, which survived only in a short reach of the Locust Fork, and has produced more than 36,000 animals for release back into the Locust Fork. The releases are part of a statewide program that since 2010 has returned over 59,000 mussels (14 species) and 102,000 snails (5 species) to Alabama rivers to re-establish extirpated populations.
stories.notes: Release reach and years not specified on the page; coordinates approximate (Locust Fork near Cleveland). Alternate background: https://www.fws.gov/story/2023-08/mussel-man

stories.title: Big Canoe Creek culvert-to-bridge replacement at Goodwin's Mill
stories.orgs: Cawaco RC&D; US Fish and Wildlife Service Partners for Fish and Wildlife; Alabama Rivers and Streams Network
stories.desc: Seven failing metal culverts that were near collapse and blocking aquatic passage on Big Canoe Creek at Goodwin's Mill were replaced with a clear-span bridge, restoring natural flow and sediment transport. Combined with the 2013 dam removal at the same site, the work reconnects about 20 miles of habitat for the trispot darter, Canoe Creek clubshell and finelined pocketbook within the Big Canoe Creek Strategic Habitat Unit.
stories.notes: May overlap with a culvert/AOP slice.

stories.title: Goodwins Mill Stream Crossing Replacement (Culverts to Bridge), Big Canoe Creek
stories.orgs: U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service Partners for Fish and Wildlife (lead); The Nature Conservancy; Cawaco Resource Conservation & Development Council; National Fish and Wildlife Foundation (funder); Alabama Rivers and Streams Network; private landowner
stories.desc: Partners replaced a failing seven-pipe metal culvert crossing on Big Canoe Creek at Goodwins Mill (the only access to a private residence) with a clear-span bridge. The buckling culverts had altered flow and blocked movement of fish and mussels; the new bridge restores natural flow and aquatic organism passage and, combined with the 2013 dam removal just upstream, reconnects roughly 20 miles of habitat for the federally listed trispot darter, Canoe Creek clubshell, finelined pocketbook and triangular kidneyshell.
stories.notes: Announced January 2026; completion year inferred as 2025. Before photo: https://alh2o.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/Before.jpg. Alternate link: https://cawaco.org/from-collapse-to-connection-big-canoe-creek-restoration-restores-flow-reconnects-habitat/

stories.title: Big Canoe Creek Endangered Mussel Reintroduction (Canoe Creek Clubshell & Coosa Moccasinshell)
stories.orgs: Alabama Aquatic Biodiversity Center (ADCNR Wildlife & Freshwater Fisheries); U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service; Big Canoe Creek Preserve Partners; Friends of Big Canoe Creek; The Nature Conservancy
stories.desc: Ten years after the Goodwin's Mill Dam removal, biologists in September 2023 released more than 250 PIT-tagged, hatchery-reared federally endangered mussels (Canoe Creek clubshell, found only in this watershed, and Coosa moccasinshell) into the reconnected reach of Big Canoe Creek. The mussels were propagated at the Alabama Aquatic Biodiversity Center in Marion from larvae of gravid wild females and grown 16-27 months before release; annual monitoring and additional stockings are planned until the populations reproduce on their own.
stories.notes: Release site is in the Big Canoe Creek watershed near Springville; exact reach not published. Coordinates approximate.

stories.title: Goodwin's Mill Dam Removal and Mussel Reintroduction, Big Canoe Creek
stories.orgs: U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service; Alabama Aquatic Biodiversity Center; Alabama Department of Conservation and Natural Resources; Friends of Big Canoe Creek; Coosa Riverkeeper; The Nature Conservancy; private landowner; The Nature Conservancy (Alabama); U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service (Alabama Ecological Services / Partners for Fish and Wildlife); Geological Survey of Alabama; private landowner (Lovell family); US Fish and Wildlife Service; Big Canoe Creek Preserve Partners
stories.desc: The Goodwin's Mill dam on Big Canoe Creek was removed in November 2013, reconnecting roughly 20 miles of upstream habitat and restoring passage for 54 fish species in the watershed. In September 2023 partners released more than 250 federally protected mussels, including Coosa moccasinshell and Canoe Creek clubshell, into the restored reach. The Coosa moccasinshell had not been recorded in the watershed since 1974; released mussels are PIT-tagged and monitored annually with the goal of self-reproducing populations.
stories.notes: County inferred from Springville/Big Canoe Creek; the story names the town but not the county. Also documented at: https://coosariver.org/removing-goodwins-mill-dam/

stories.title: Trispot Darter Culvert Replacements, Little Canoe Creek
stories.orgs: U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service (National Fish Passage Program; Alabama Ecological Services Field Office; Partners for Fish and Wildlife); CAWACO RC&D Council; Manulife Investment Management; St. Clair County; City of Springville; private landowners
stories.desc: Undersized and failing concrete/corrugated-steel culverts on Little Canoe Creek and a tributary were replaced with bottomless arch structures, with up to three road crossings in the package and about 6 stream miles reconnected. The first crossing, on private timberland managed by Manulife, was completed with Bipartisan Infrastructure Law funds and restored a natural stream grade for the federally threatened trispot darter; the fine-lined pocketbook mussel was found during the work. The new structures also cut road flooding and reduced flood cleanup costs at a city sports complex.
stories.notes: FWS project page lists status Active with 6 stream miles as an accomplishment; first culvert completed, additional crossings planned. Companion story with before/after photos: https://www.fws.gov/story/2023-05/team-wins-big-alabama . Project is also a case study in the FWS 'Healthy Rivers, Communities and Economies' report (2024).

stories.title: Black Branch and Cane Creek acid mine drainage remediation (Oakman)
stories.orgs: Alabama Dept. of Industrial Relations Abandoned Mine Lands Program; ADEM; US EPA; Black Warrior Clean Water Partnership
stories.desc: Between 2006 and 2011 the Abandoned Mine Lands program and ADEM ($810K AML + $255K Section 319) backfilled a collapsed mine subsidence with limestone riprap, relocated and capped a coal gob pile with 1-2 feet of soil, and built a passive vertical-flow treatment system on Red Branch to neutralize acid mine drainage feeding Black Branch and Cane Creek. By 2012 pH was within the 6.0-8.5 standard and in 2014 ADEM delisted Black Branch (siltation, metals) and 18 miles of Cane Creek (metals, nutrients, pH, OE/DO, siltation).
stories.water: Black Branch / Cane Creek (Black Warrior basin)
stories.notes: EPA NPS success story.

stories.title: Seven Springs / Godsey Easement Watercress Darter Habitat Restoration (Culvert Fix, Invasive Removal, Dump Cleanup)
stories.orgs: Freshwater Land Trust; Black Warrior Riverkeeper; U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service; Action Environmental; private landowner (Emily Godsey)
stories.desc: On a 26.1-acre conservation easement in Birmingham's Powderly neighborhood containing 228 ft of Seven Springs (one of only five or six known watercress darter sites) and 1,142 ft of Nabors Branch, partners in fall 2023 corrected a perched culvert under 24th Street SW that had blocked endangered watercress darters from moving upstream, then in 2024 mulched and treated Chinese privet, mimosa, Bradford pear and autumn olive to return sunlight to the spring run, and in 2025 removed 1,416 tires and 129 tons of dumped trash and blocked dumping access. The work restored upstream fish access and the open-canopy conditions that support the aquatic vegetation darters need; the newly described Birmingham darter was also documented on the site.
stories.water: Seven Springs / Nabors Branch (Valley Creek, Black Warrior basin)
stories.notes: Stewardship funded by supplemental environmental projects from Riverkeeper lawsuits. Freshwater Land Trust's own post on the 2023 culvert project (https://freshwaterlandtrust.org/2023/11/flt-and-partners-complete-stream-restoration-project-in-west-birmingham/) was listed on FLT's news index but could not be fetched (provenance block). Easement announcement: https://blackwarriorriver.org/big-win-for-watercress-darters/

stories.title: Seven Springs Watercress Darter Sanctuary at Faith Apostolic Church
stories.orgs: Freshwater Land Trust; Faith Apostolic Church (landowner); U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service (Ecological Services, Partners for Fish and Wildlife, Refuge System); Samford University Department of Biology; Southern Environmental Center; Birmingham-Southern College; Faith Apostolic Church; US Fish and Wildlife Service; NFWF Five Star
stories.desc: After Samford biologists discovered a watercress darter population in Seven Springs in 2002, Freshwater Land Trust and Faith Apostolic Church signed a 2005 agreement creating a nature sanctuary, meditation garden and outdoor classroom around the spring run, with native plantings and habitat improvements funded in part by a Five Star grant and a USFWS-supported 'ecoscape' with a darter mural. USFWS reports the darter population at the site is thriving, and student research there has informed adaptive management of the spring.
stories.notes: Adjacent to and upstream of the Godsey easement site. Alternate description: https://www.fws.gov/project/urban-darter-program

stories.title: Glenn Springs Watercress Darter Habitat Restoration (Privet Removal), Bessemer
stories.orgs: U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service Alabama Ecological Services; Partners for Fish and Wildlife; Alabama Rivers and Streams Network; Glenn Springs neighborhood association (landowner); University of Alabama at Birmingham students; REI; Freshwater Land Trust
stories.desc: As part of a three-year, $247,000 USFWS-led effort to improve all five known urban spring sites of the endangered watercress darter around Birmingham, volunteers spent two days in late 2020 mechanically clearing dense Chinese privet that had shaded out the aquatic vegetation at Glenn Springs in Bessemer. Opening the canopy restored sunlight to the spring run and the submerged plants the darters depend on, with educational signage and quarterly Endangered Species Tours following.
stories.notes: Coordinates approximate (Bessemer). Related FLT post 'Volunteers Enhance Endangered Species Habitat in Bessemer' (Dec 2020) could not be fetched.

stories.title: Alabama Aquatic Biodiversity Center Statewide Mussel and Snail Reintroduction Program
stories.orgs: Alabama Department of Conservation and Natural Resources (Wildlife & Freshwater Fisheries); U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service; Alabama Power; Alabama Rivers and Streams Network; Tennessee Wildlife Resources Agency; The Nature Conservancy
stories.desc: Established in 2004-2006 at the former USGS aquaculture station in Marion, the AABC is the largest state nongame mollusk recovery program in the U.S.; since 2010 it has propagated and released more than 59,000 mussels of 14 species (12 federally listed) and 102,000 snails of 5 species into roughly 20 Alabama rivers and streams, starting with Mobile River basin species at the Coosa River below Weiss Dam. Reintroduced populations are now documented reproducing in the Paint Rock River, Bear Creek and Big Canoe Creek.
stories.water: Cahaba River (facility); releases in Coosa, Paint Rock, Locust Fork, Bear Creek and others
stories.notes: Program-level entry located at the hatchery; individual release sites are entered separately where documented. Caller may drop if only site-specific projects are wanted.

stories.title: Mill Creek urban stream restoration and LID (Smiths Station / Phenix City)
stories.orgs: Alabama Cooperative Extension System; ADEM; Auburn University; Cities of Smiths Station and Phenix City; Lee and Russell Counties; Lee County Board of Education; UGA Extension; Columbus Water Works; Alabama Water Watch; Chattahoochee River Warden; Phenix City Beautiful; Alabama Power; Alabama Clean Water Partnership; NFWF Five Star
stories.desc: Two Section 319 phases (2011-2016; $535K federal, $433K match, $50K NFWF) in the 9.93-mile Mill Creek watershed (Chattahoochee River) built three stream restorations, streambank stabilization, constructed stormwater wetlands, bioretention cells, rain gardens with cisterns and vegetated swales, with a septic pump-out program and school outreach. EPT taxa rose from one (1999) to eight (2014), the macroinvertebrate rating improved to fair, and ADEM delisted Mill Creek in 2018 for low DO/organic enrichment.

stories.title: Removal of the Elba Hydroelectric Dam
stories.orgs: U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service (National Fish Passage Program); Choctawhatchee, Pea and Yellow Rivers Watershed Management Authority; Town of Elba
stories.desc: Removal of the inoperable Elba Hydroelectric Dam, described by FWS as the only fish passage barrier in the Choctawhatchee River basin and a navigation hazard, contaminant source and flood-risk contributor for the town of Elba. The $1.93 million National Fish Passage Program project is expected to increase access to habitat types used by threatened and endangered fish and mussels in the watershed by about 29 percent.
stories.notes: FY2024 National Fish Passage Program award; project page uses future tense and reports no completed accomplishments, so treat as in progress. No project-specific photo on the page (generic banner only).

stories.title: Twelve Mile Creek bank stabilization and Langan Lake restoration (Three Mile Creek watershed, Mobile)
stories.orgs: City of Mobile; University of South Alabama; Mobile Bay National Estuary Program; ADEM; MAWSS; Village of Spring Hill; ADCNR; RESTORE Act; McCrory & Williams; James H. Adams & Son; McElhaney Construction; Geosyntec; Hughes Companies
stories.desc: Phases 1 and 2 (complete) stabilized the banks and bed of Twelve Mile Creek from East Drive to Langan Park Lake using in-stream structures that slow stormwater, protect undercut sewer crossings and add habitat, ending chronic sediment delivery to the lake. Phase 3 (2025-2027) is dredging Langan Lake and naturalizing a concrete channel to aid flood control and island apple snail abatement.
stories.water: Twelve Mile Creek / Three Mile Creek (Langan Lake)
stories.notes: Feet of stream restored not published.

stories.title: Joes Branch step-pool stream restoration (D'Olive Creek watershed)
stories.orgs: Mobile Bay National Estuary Program; ADEM; NFWF Gulf Environmental Benefit Fund; US EPA Region 4; Mississippi-Alabama Sea Grant; City of Daphne; City of Spanish Fort; Baldwin County; Thompson Engineering; Alabama Power; Lake Forest POA; Westminster Village; ALDOT; North State Environmental; Southern Excavators; Geological Survey of Alabama
stories.desc: On the 1.57-mile Joes Branch in Spanish Fort and Daphne, partners built regenerative step-pool conveyance systems (JB1, JB2 and a connecting transition reach, about 1,400 feet) to stop an active headcut, plus wetland restoration, floodplain realignment and two detention-pond retrofits, with about $920K in Section 319 funds, $712K match and nearly $3M from NFWF's $12M D'Olive watershed commitment. Sediment loading dropped 90-95 percent, median TSS fell to 7 mg/L and ADEM removed Joes Branch from the 303(d) list for siltation in 2020.
stories.notes: Part of the larger NFWF-funded D'Olive Creek/Tiawasee Creek restoration program coordinated by Mobile Bay NEP.

stories.title: Dixon property oyster-castle living shoreline (Mobile Bay)
stories.orgs: Alabama Coastal Foundation; US Fish and Wildlife Service; University of South Alabama; Dauphin Island Sea Lab; Murphy High School; Bishop State Community College; NFWF; US Army Corps of Engineers (permit)
stories.desc: On an eroding private bayfront in Mobile, a teacher-led partnership built five oyster-castle block reefs (three before 2020 and two in June 2022 using 80 blocks each) with DISL summer students and NFWF funding, with Spartina marsh planting scheduled after hurricane season. The reefs are intended to dampen waves and rebuild marsh fringe on the residential shoreline.
stories.notes: Small demonstration site; exact location not published, coordinates approximate.

stories.title: Caney Branch livestock exclusion and pathogen delisting (Weeks Bay watershed)
stories.orgs: ADEM; USDA NRCS; EPA Gulf of Mexico Program; Geological Survey of Alabama; Baldwin County SWCD; Weeks Bay NERR and Weeks Bay Foundation; ADCNR; USFWS; Dauphin Island Sea Lab; University of South Alabama; Alabama Clean Water Partnership; landowners
stories.desc: Under the Fish River/Weeks Bay Watershed Project ($450K Section 319, $158K Gulf of Mexico Program, $114K landowner match), ranchers along the 5-mile Caney Branch installed livestock exclusion fencing, hardened stream crossings and riparian buffers, backed by cleanups, field days and workshops. In 2001 all 22 ADEM fecal coliform samples met criteria and the segment was removed from the 303(d) list in 2002.
stories.notes: Exact reach not given; coordinates approximate within the Fish River watershed.

stories.title: Deer River Shoreline Stabilization
stories.orgs: National Fish and Wildlife Foundation (Gulf Environmental Benefit Fund); Alabama Department of Conservation and Natural Resources
stories.desc: A two-phase GEBF project stabilizing the eroding shoreline of Deer River on the western shore of Mobile Bay, protecting marsh habitat from wave-driven erosion. Phase I was awarded in 2018 and phase II in 2021.
stories.notes: Award year from the GEBF project list; location approximate.

stories.title: Alabama Oyster Gardening Program reef enhancement
stories.orgs: Alabama Cooperative Extension System; Auburn University; Mississippi-Alabama Sea Grant Consortium; ADCNR Marine Resources Division; volunteer waterfront gardeners
stories.desc: Since 2001 volunteer oyster gardeners in Mobile and Baldwin counties have grown juvenile oysters in cages off private docks and transplanted them to public reefs in Mobile Bay and Mississippi Sound. The program has produced more than 940,000 oysters and enhanced over 46.5 acres of reef.
stories.notes: Figures from the 2021 Coastal Alabama Comprehensive Oyster Restoration Strategy.

stories.title: Baker Branch LID restoration and delisting (Fish River watershed)
stories.orgs: Baldwin County SWCD; Alabama Cooperative Extension System; ADEM; USDA NRCS; EPA Gulf of Mexico Program; Geological Survey of Alabama; Weeks Bay NERR; Mobile Bay NEP; The Nature Conservancy; Baldwin County Commission; NFWF
stories.desc: A CWA Section 319-funded project (2007-2010) installed bioretention areas, a rain garden and rainwater-harvesting devices in the 6.15-mile Baker Branch tributary of the Fish River, building on three decades of Fish River/Weeks Bay watershed work. Post-restoration monitoring in 2018 showed dissolved oxygen above the 5 mg/L standard and Baker Branch was removed from Alabama's 303(d) list in 2020 for low DO/organic enrichment.
stories.notes: EPA NPS success story PDF; work was mainly stormwater LID rather than in-channel.

stories.title: Lower Fish River Watershed Restoration
stories.orgs: National Fish and Wildlife Foundation (Gulf Environmental Benefit Fund); Alabama Department of Conservation and Natural Resources; Mobile Bay National Estuary Program
stories.desc: A two-phase Gulf Environmental Benefit Fund project restoring the lower Fish River watershed above Weeks Bay, combining streambank and shoreline work with wetland and riparian restoration to cut the sediment and nutrient loads reaching the bay. Awards were made in 2020 and 2022.
stories.notes: Scope and year taken from the NFWF GEBF project list and phase I fact sheet; award year, not necessarily completion year.

stories.title: Alabama Coastal Foundation oyster shell recycling and reef restoration
stories.orgs: Alabama Coastal Foundation; National Fish and Wildlife Foundation; participating restaurants; ADCNR
stories.desc: Launched in 2016 with NFWF funding, ACF collects shell from coastal Alabama restaurants, cures it and returns it to Alabama waters as cultch for reefs and living shorelines. As of October 2026 the program reports 31.5 million shells recycled and 120 acres of oyster reef restored in Mobile and Baldwin county waters.
stories.notes: Deployment sites not itemized on the page; coordinates are a coastal centroid.

stories.title: Fowl River Coastal Spits and Wetlands Restoration
stories.orgs: National Fish and Wildlife Foundation (Gulf Environmental Benefit Fund); Alabama Department of Conservation and Natural Resources; Mobile Bay National Estuary Program
stories.desc: GEBF-funded restoration of eroding coastal marsh spits and wetlands on the lower Fowl River, using placed material and wave-attenuation structures to rebuild marsh and protect adjacent seagrass. Phase I was awarded in 2016 and a further phase in 2021.
stories.notes: Related to the Mobile Bay NEP Fowl River marsh spit project already in this dataset; award year from the GEBF list.

stories.title: Fowl River marsh spit and shoreline restoration (Theodore)
stories.orgs: Mobile Bay National Estuary Program; Thompson Engineering; US Army Corps of Engineers (dredged material); ADCNR; RESTORE/NFWF funding
stories.desc: MBNEP is restoring five eroding wetland spits (28 acres) on the lower Fowl River using 136,000 cubic yards of beneficially reused dredged material placed in thin layers, 10,000 linear feet of timber wave-attenuation breakwaters, 791 cubic yards of riprap and 37,000 feet of coir logs and hay bales to protect the spits and adjacent seagrass beds. Bids were taken in December 2023 and construction began the following July.
stories.notes: Construction notice: https://www.mobilebaynep.com/news/major-fowl-river-project-to-begin-in-july-public-safety-advisory-for-boaters-and-recreational-users ; completion not confirmed.

stories.title: Oyster Cultch Relief and Reef Configuration study reefs (Denton Reef and East Fowl River)
stories.orgs: ADCNR Marine Resources Division; Alabama Trustee Implementation Group (Deepwater Horizon NRDA)
stories.desc: Under AL TIG Restoration Plan II, the Marine Resources Division built six cured-shell and limestone mounds (45 cubic yards) on Denton (Whitehouse) Reef and three 120-foot elongated mounds plus controls on a 2014 reef site near East Fowl River, completing construction in 2020 to test whether vertical relief and configuration improve oyster recruitment and survival. NOAA lists the project as complete with monitoring ongoing.
stories.water: Mobile Bay (Denton Reef, East Fowl River)
stories.notes: NOAA project record https://www.gulfspillrestoration.noaa.gov/project?id=136 (Complete). Coordinates approximate.

stories.title: Wolf Creek Headwaters Restoration
stories.orgs: National Fish and Wildlife Foundation (Gulf Environmental Benefit Fund); Alabama Department of Conservation and Natural Resources
stories.desc: A two-phase GEBF project restoring the headwaters of Wolf Creek in coastal Alabama, addressing erosion and hydrologic damage in the upper watershed to improve water quality and habitat downstream. Awards were made in 2020 and 2022.
stories.notes: Location approximate. Award year from the GEBF project list.

stories.title: Alabama living shorelines program (TNC and partners, 17 sites, 9+ miles)
stories.orgs: The Nature Conservancy; ADCNR Marine Resources Division; Mobile Bay NEP; Dauphin Island Sea Lab; NOAA; NFWF; volunteers
stories.desc: Since 2005 TNC, the Marine Resources Division and partners have built living shorelines at 17 locations along the Alabama coast totaling more than 9 miles, using bagged shell, limestone, reef blocks and marsh plantings with more than $28 million invested and 1,868 volunteers. Sites include Helen Wood Park, Alabama Port, Coffee Island, Swift Tract and Lightning Point; several of the early oyster-shell structures were later replaced with rock breakwaters.
stories.notes: Program-level summary from the 2021 Coastal Alabama Comprehensive Oyster Restoration Strategy; individual site pages no longer online.

stories.title: Lightning Point Shoreline and Marsh Restoration, Bayou La Batre
stories.orgs: The Nature Conservancy in Alabama; City of Bayou La Batre; Mobile County; Alabama Department of Conservation and Natural Resources; National Fish and Wildlife Foundation; Dauphin Island Sea Lab; Moffatt & Nichol; University of Alabama-Birmingham; Alma Bryant High School; The Nature Conservancy; NFWF Gulf Environmental Benefit Fund; ADCNR; Mobile Bay NEP; University of Alabama at Birmingham
stories.desc: At the mouth of the Bayou La Batre navigation channel, TNC and partners built roughly 1.5 miles of overlapping segmented rock breakwaters and two jetties (about 57,000 tons of rock) and created about 40 acres of intertidal marsh, scrub-shrub upland and tidal flat from more than 300,000 cubic meters of repurposed dredged material. Crews excavated over 10,000 meters of tidal creeks, planted 90,000 native plants and placed more than 600 cubic yards of recycled oyster shell, expanding the shoreline by over 600 feet across a roughly 170-acre project area. Oystercatchers, black skimmers and nesting least terns colonized the site during construction, more than 50 bird species have been recorded, the structures survived five named storms, and an economic analysis estimates $67 million in benefits from the $21 million investment.
stories.notes: Construction began fall 2019; 7 of 11 breakwaters, 2 jetties and 40+ acres of habitat were complete by the 2020 hurricane season, with the final four breakwaters following a 2024 land acquisition. County inferred (Mobile County is a named partner and landowner).

stories.title: Swift Tract living shoreline breakwaters (Bon Secour Bay, Weeks Bay NERR)
stories.orgs: Alabama Deepwater Horizon NRDA Trustees (ADCNR, NOAA, USFWS); Weeks Bay National Estuarine Research Reserve; The Nature Conservancy
stories.desc: A $5M Deepwater Horizon Phase III early-restoration project placed rock breakwaters along about 1.6 miles of eroding Bon Secour Bay shoreline on the state-owned Swift Tract beginning September 30, 2016, extending a half-mile living shoreline TNC built there in 2011. The breakwaters reduce erosion of the marsh shoreline and were designed to develop about three acres of intertidal oyster reef; the project is now in long-term monitoring.
stories.notes: NOAA project record: https://www.gulfspillrestoration.noaa.gov/project?id=12 (status Monitoring/O&M). Weeks Bay stewardship photo: https://www.outdooralabama.com/sites/default/files/styles/content_slide_image/public/Weeks%20Bay%20Reserve/Stewardship/Swift%20tract%20living%20shoreline.JPG?itok=TCMYZiOL

stories.title: Salt Aire Shoreline Restoration
stories.orgs: National Fish and Wildlife Foundation (Gulf Environmental Benefit Fund); Alabama Department of Conservation and Natural Resources; Mobile County
stories.desc: GEBF-funded shoreline restoration at the Salt Aire property on Mobile Bay, carried out alongside a conservation acquisition, to stabilize eroding bay shoreline and restore fringing marsh habitat. Awarded in 2017.
stories.notes: Award year from the GEBF project list; location approximate.
